interface.name: afar_appmenu_manager_v1

description.summary: publish a menu for an xdg toplevel

interface.description: This global lets an application associate a com.canonical.dbusmenu object on the session bus with one of its xdg toplevels.

entry.name: already_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a menu object

entry.name: invalid_toplevel
entry.summary: the toplevel is no longer available

request.name: get_menu
request.description: There can be at most one live afar_appmenu_v1 per xdg_toplevel. Creating a second association raises already_exists. The association starts without an address. It may be created before initial mapping.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Menu objects created by the manager remain valid.

interface.name: afar_appmenu_v1
interface.description: The application starts in local mode. The association is scoped to the xdg_toplevel role, and the advertised address survives unmap and remap. Unmapping revokes global presentation. Destroying the toplevel makes this object inert until the client destroys it.

entry.name: invalid_address
entry.summary: invalid D-Bus name or object path

entry.name: local
entry.summary: the application presents its menu locally

entry.name: global
entry.summary: a shell has taken responsibility for the menu

request.name: set_address
request.description:
The D-Bus object must already be exported. This request replaces the previous address immediately and resets presentation to local. It does not wait for wl_surface.commit. Malformed addresses raise invalid_address.
The serial is chosen by the client and echoed in presentation events. Use a different serial for each update that could still have an event in flight. Apply presentation events for the latest serial only.

request.name: clear
request.description: The address is withdrawn immediately and presentation returns to local for this update. The serial has the same semantics as set_address.

event.name: presentation
event.description: Local presentation is reported for each set_address or clear request. Global presentation means a shell has accepted responsibility for this published menu. It does not indicate that the window currently has focus. The compositor reports local when that responsibility ends.
